```text
10 passed
```

Pre-commit checks for the modified files passed.

Runtime smoke test on NVIDIA A100 40GB:

* V2 engine initialized successfully with `enable_jit_warmup=False`
* Two consecutive greedy generations completed successfully
* Output token IDs were identical
* First request: 76.875 ms
* Second request: 45.129 ms

commits.pr_title: [MRV2] Release weight offloader on shutdown
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

MRV2 leaves its process-global `PrefetchOffloader` alive after in-process shutdown, retaining model layers, pinned CPU weights, and GPU staging buffers. Reset it after device synchronization so the existing teardown can reclaim those resources before another engine starts.

## Reproducer

Save as `/tmp/repro_mrv2_offloader_shutdown.py`:

```python
import gc
import weakref
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from vllm.model_executor.offloader import (
    PrefetchOffloader,
    get_offloader,
    set_offloader,
)
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner import GPUModelRunner

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 2))
buffer = torch.ones(1)
refs = [weakref.ref(model[0]), weakref.ref(model[0].weight), weakref.ref(buffer)]

offloader = PrefetchOffloader.__new__(PrefetchOffloader)
offloader.module_offloaders = [SimpleNamespace(module=model[0])]
offloader.buffer_pool = SimpleNamespace(_buffers={"weight": [buffer]})
offloader.prefetch_step = 1
offloader._hook_module_forward(0, model[0])
set_offloader(offloader)

runner = GPUModelRunner.__new__(GPUModelRunner)
runner.model = model
runner.speculator = None
runner.cudagraph_manager = None
runner.fast_prefill = None
runner.vllm_config = SimpleNamespace()
del model, buffer, offloader

with (
    patch("vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner.torch.accelerator.synchronize"),
    patch("vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner.torch.accelerator.empty_cache"),
    patch("vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner.free_before_shutdown"),
):
    runner.shutdown()

gc.collect()
print(type(get_offloader()).__name__)
print([ref() is not None for ref in refs])
```

Run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python /tmp/repro_mrv2_offloader_shutdown.py
```

### Main

```text
PrefetchOffloader
[True, True, True]
```

### This branch

```text
NoopOffloader
[False, False, False]
```
## Test Plan

CPU and static checks:

```text

.venv/bin/python /tmp/check_mrv2_offloader_shutdown_idempotence.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py --hook-stage manual
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] batch_invariant: keep non-AllReduce collectives enabled on NCCL >= 2.31
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `override_envs_for_invariance()` sets `NCCL_ALGO=allreduce:tree` and `NCCL_PROTO=Simple`. On NCCL 2.31 that pair leaves every collective other than AllReduce with no algorithm, and any TP>1 or PP>1 engine fails at warmup:

```
No algorithm/protocol nor symKernelId available for function Broadcast with datatype ncclInt8.
NCCL_ALGO was set to allreduce:tree. NCCL_PROTO was set to Simple.
torch.distributed.DistBackendError: NCCL error ... invalid usage
```

(TP fails on the pynccl `ncclAllGather` in the logits gather, PP on `torch.distributed.broadcast` in `pp_utils.py`.)

NCCL 2.31 zero-fills the per-collective algorithm table whenever `NCCL_ALGO` is set and re-enables only the collectives the string names (`src/tuning/cost_model.cc`, `ncclTuningCostModelInit`). The zeroed rows are consulted only for collectives NCCL marks "forced", and the prefix-less `NCCL_PROTO=Simple` forces all of them. NCCL 2.30 left unnamed collectives enabled, which this setting relied on. PyPI `nvidia-nccl-cu12` is already 2.31.2, so this bites as soon as the torch pin moves.

## Change

`NCCL_ALGO="ring,tree;allreduce:tree"`: re-enable Ring and Tree for every collective, then pin AllReduce to Tree. Same selection as before on NCCL 2.30 (Ring for Broadcast/AllGather/ReduceScatter, Tree for AllReduce), so determinism is unaffected.

## Test Plan

2-GPU `torch.distributed` probe, one collective per process, under the exact env set of `override_envs_for_invariance()`:

| NCCL | env | allreduce | broadcast | allgather | reducescatter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.31.2 | current (`allreduce:tree`) | OK | FAIL | FAIL | FAIL |
| 2.31.2 | this PR | OK | OK | OK | OK |
| 2.30.7 | current | OK | OK | OK | OK |
| 2.30.7 | this PR | OK | OK | OK | OK |

Identical on H100-class (sm90), GB200 (sm100) and GB300 (sm103). Leave-one-out over the env set confirms `NCCL_ALGO` + `NCCL_PROTO` is the necessary and sufficient pair.

## Test Result

End to end with `vllm serve` (Llama-3-8B bf16, `--enforce-eager`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`) on GB200 with NCCL 2.31.2: TP=2 and PP=2 both die at warmup on the current code and both come up and answer `/v1/completions` with this change (same node, same model, patch as the only difference).

Side note, not changed here: NCCL rejects `NCCL_NTHREADS=1` (`must be a multiple of 32`) and ignores it.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Fuse the inverse RoPE into the sparse decode reduce
commits.pr_body: ## Purpose The ROCm sparse decode writes the attention output twice. The reduce kernel combines the split-K partials and stores `[T, H, 512]`, and then `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` reads that whole tensor back, rotates the trailing 64 rope lanes and writes it out again — a full round trip per layer, for an epilogue on data the reduce already held in registers. From a 10-step decode trace on MI355X (TP4, rank 0): | kernel | total | calls | share of kernel time | |---|---|---|---| | `_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_partial_kernel` | 4707.3 us | 430 | 3.24% | | `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` | 2214.2 us | 430 | 1.52% | | `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` | 1965.5 us | 430 | 1.35% | 430 = 43 layers x 10 steps: every layer pays it, sliding-window and MTP layers included. FlashMLA's mega-attention kernel already folds this rotation and the FP8 cast into its epilogue on SM100 — `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` describes exactly that — and the layer interface for it is platform-generic (`_alloc_attn_out` / `_o_proj`, `accepts_unnormed_unroped_query`). The ROCm Triton path just never took it. ## What changes The reduce gained an optional inverse-RoPE epilogue. Reshaping the combined row into adjacent pairs puts the rope lanes in the last 32 of 256 pairs, so giving the NoPE pairs cos=1 and sin=0 lets one expression cover the whole row with no branch and no second pass: ```python even, odd = tl.split(tl.reshape(out, (BLOCK_H, COMB_DIM // 2, 2))) out = tl.reshape(tl.join(even * cos + odd * sin, odd * cos - even * sin), ...) ``` Which rows still owe a rotation depends on the batch: the reduce rotates the decode rows it produces, prefill rows have no such epilogue, and a decode path that does not fuse (for instance the opt-in HIP kernel in #57282) rotates nothing. `rocm_sparse_attn_decode` reports how many leading rows it rotated and `forward_mqa` pays the standalone pass for the rest, in place. On a decode-only step that leaves nothing to do, so the kernel does not launch at all rather than being replaced by a copy. That bookkeeping belongs in the eager attention segment specifically, not in `_o_proj`. An earlier revision of this PR handed the row count to `_o_proj`, which runs inside the compiled region; since vLLM compiles with `skip_all_guards_unsafe`, the Python int froze at its trace-time value and rows ended up rotated zero or two times. GSM8K fell to 0.087 against a 0.902 baseline with fluent output and no error of any kind. The lane arithmetic was correct throughout, so no kernel-level test caught it -- only the eval did. Two side effects worth noting: the rotation now happens on the fp32 accumulator rather than the already-rounded bf16 output, dropping a rounding step, and the NoPE lanes come through bit-exact (x1.0 + 0.0). Expected effect: ~196 us and 43 launches per step removed, ~1.35% of decode GPU time on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. ## Not a duplicate - #54894 fuses inverse RoPE with group quantization via AITER's `inverse_rope_group_quant` — different model (`deepseek_v4`), different mechanism, and it keeps the rotation as its own pass. This removes the pass. The two are compatible in direction: if the V4.1 ROCm path later adopts an FP8 `wo_a`, the natural next step is emitting the FP8 cast from this same epilogue, which is what the SM100 kernel does. - #57282 adds an opt-in HIP decode kernel for a specific batch range and falls through to this Triton path otherwise; the two compose, and the rotated-row count above is what keeps them honest. - #56720 and #56342 touch other kernels in the same file, not the reduce. ## Test results Unit tests, on the branch, MI355X: ``` $ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py \ tests/kernels/attention/test_dsv41_rocm_fused_inv_rope.py -q 69 passed in 38.64s ``` Kernel equivalence, MI355X: running the real decode kernels fused, then unfused followed by `_fused_inverse_rope_gptj`, on identical inputs. NoPE lanes are bit-exact and rope lanes agree to bf16 rounding at every shape tried -- `(queries, heads)` of (2, 3), (1, 128), (8, 128), (32, 128): | | max abs diff | |---|---| | NoPE lanes | 0.0 (32 queries: 4.9e-4) | | rope lanes | <= 2.0e-3, against \|rope\| up to 0.29 | Decode capture, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 on MI355X, 10 engine steps at concurrency 1, MTP spec decode. Per-step kernel time, mean over the four TP ranks: | kernel | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` | 201.6 us | 0.0 us (430 launches -> 0) | | `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` | 218.7 us | 227.0 us | The pass disappears on decode-only steps and the reduce absorbs it for 8.3 us, so 193 us per step net, against the 196 us the trace analysis predicted. Accuracy, GSM8K 5-shot, greedy, concurrency 32 score remains the same --- AI assistance was used to write this change. I have reviewed every line, ran the tests and evals above myself, and am responsible for it.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] hadacore_transform: respect inplace parameter to fix garbage outputs with QuIP transforms
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix garbage outputs from QuIP transforms on Blackwell GPUs under `torch.compile` + CUDA graph capture. Initially observed on RTX 5090 (SM120); since reproduced on B200 (SM100) with the v0.21.0 prebuilt wheel + torch 2.11.0. Addresses the runtime side of vllm-project/llm-compressor#2006.

## Background

The `hadacore_transform` op is declared with a mutable schema:

```cpp
ops.def("hadacore_transform(Tensor! x, bool inplace) -> Tensor");
```

Two interacting issues:

**1. Kernel ignores the `inplace` parameter (latent bug).** In `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/hadamard/hadacore/hadamard_transform_cuda.cu`, the kernel always writes to `x.data_ptr()` regardless of `inplace`:

```cpp
torch::stable::Tensor out = inplace ? x : torch::stable::empty_like(x);
hadacore::run_fht<SCALAR_TYPE>(x.data_ptr(), x.data_ptr(), x.numel(), ...);
// `inplace=False` callers receive `out`, but `out` was never written to
return torch::stable::reshape(out, res_shape);
```

The conditional copy-back cannot fire because `out` is only aliased to `x` when `inplace=True`. The path is currently unused in vLLM but is publicly exposed.

**2. Mutable schema causes inductor to elide protective clones.** In `CompressedTensorsLinearTransformMethod.apply()`, the `.clone()` introduced in #26849 for compile robustness:

```python
x[:, start:start+length] = self.output_transform(
    x[:, start:start+length].clone(), part_id=part_id
)
```

Inductor analyzes the `Tensor!` schema, decides the clone is redundant (the op will mutate anyway), and elides it from the FX graph (verified via `TORCH_LOGS="output_code"`). The kernel ends up receiving a slice view aliasing `x`, producing garbage outputs under `torch.compile` + cudagraph. Initially observed on SM120; later also reproduced on B200 (SM100) with the v0.21.0 prebuilt wheel + torch 2.11.0 (QuIP variants: WikiText-2 PPL ~1.4e6; coherent with `enforce_eager=True`). @mgoin's `gsm8k_eval` in #28748 (0.697) used a combination that does not trigger the inductor elision: whether the bug manifests depends on the (torch version x compile/cudagraph) configuration, not the hardware.

| Test | Hardware | Pre-fix | Post-fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| W4A16 + QuIP, compile | RTX 5090 | ❌ Garbage | ✅ Coherent |
| NVFP4A16 + QuIP, compile | RTX 5090 | ❌ Garbage | ✅ Coherent |
| NVFP4A16 only, compile | RTX 5090 | ✅ Coherent | ✅ Byte-identical |
| NVFP4A16 + QuIP, cudagraph, v0.21.0 wheel + torch 2.11 | B200 | ❌ Garbage (PPL ~1.4e6) | N/A |
| Same, `enforce_eager=True` | B200 | ✅ Coherent (6.84) | N/A |
| Kernel sanity (`inplace=True` vs `False`) | B200 | N/A | ✅ max diff 0.0 |
| `gsm8k_eval` @mgoin SpinQuant model | B200 | 0.697 (#28748) | 0.697 |

## Changes

Kernel writes to `out.data_ptr()` instead of `x.data_ptr()` (respects `inplace`); call sites in `module.py` pass `inplace=False` to opt into the non-aliasing path. The existing `.clone()` from #26849 is retained as a defensive layer.

## Reproduction

The bug manifests on any compressed-tensors checkpoint using online Hadamard transforms (QuIP) under vLLM's default `torch.compile` + cudagraph execution. The root cause is in the kernel, independent of the calibration path. It also blocks the MXFP4 W4A4 + MR-GPTQ path (where rotations contribute ~+3 pts PPL recovery vs GPTQ alone on Llama-3.1-8B) and any future recipe relying on online Hadamard rotations.

### Step 1: produce a QuIP-transformed checkpoint

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor
cd llm-compressor
pip install -e .

# QuIP + GPTQ + NVFP4A16 example from vllm-project/llm-compressor#2751 (~10 min):
gh pr checkout 2751
python examples/transform/nvfp4_quip_gptq_example.py
# produces Llama-3.1-8B-quip-gptq-nvfp4a16
```

The attached logs were produced with an equivalent minimal datafree variant (`examples/transform/quip_example.py` adapted to the NVFP4A16 scheme, on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, producing `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quip-nvfp4a16`). Both recipes trigger the same bug.

### Step 2: reproduce the failure on `main`

```bash
# vLLM main branch build (per-commit nightly wheel; the version string embeds the main commit)
pip install vllm==0.22.1rc1.dev255+g4dcd10eb0 --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly

VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 python validate_nvfp4_quip.py <checkpoint_dir>
```

(`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` works around an unrelated FlashInfer sampler init failure on SM120 with this build; it does not affect the transform path.)

`validate_nvfp4_quip.py` is a minimal 5-prompt sanity script (greedy, `max_tokens=80`, vLLM defaults, no `enforce_eager`):

<details>
<summary>validate_nvfp4_quip.py</summary>

```python
import sys
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Engram] Fall back when /dev/shm is absent before sharing tables
commits.pr_body:
Follow-up to #57651. `can_share_engram_tables` called `shutil.disk_usage("/dev/shm")` unguarded, so a host without `/dev/shm` raised `FileNotFoundError` at model construction instead of falling back to per-rank tables. This checks `os.path.isdir(SHM_PATH)` first and reuses `SHM_PATH` from `shm_broadcast` for the remaining `/dev/shm` references. No duplicate PR covers this. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

Also flattens `DPSharedEngramStorage._allocate` while touching it: the nested try/except, the `stage` tracker and the manual `finalizer()`/`mapping.close()` rollback become one try/except around the mmap+register step. On a peer failure the locals are dropped (`del tensor, owner, mapping`), so the owner's finalizer unregisters the pages and the mapping unmaps in the same order as before. Error messages carry the exception text instead of a stage prefix. No behavior change.

Test: `pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py tests/test_config.py -k "shm or shared_memory or engram"` -> passed
Test: `pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -k shared_across_dp_replicas` (4x GB200, covers the create/open/mmap/register/pinned failure injections and the mapping lifetime checks) -> 2 passed on the flattened `_allocate`

### Model evaluation

Evaluated with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` at revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277` on one 4x GB200 node using DEP4 (`TP1 x DP4`, expert parallel) and DSpark with 5 speculative tokens and adaptive verification. MQA GSM8K 5-shot ran through the Completions API with `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, concurrency 32, and all 1,319 examples. It achieved `0.9325` flexible exact match and `0.9325` strict exact match with 0 request errors in 107.46 seconds. `dp_shared_memory=True` initialized successfully, and both Engram tables were shared across all four DP replicas (`94.42 GiB` per table/layer).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Avoid NaN in the Triton softcap for large attention logits
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56578 

`apply_softcap` computed `x * tanh(S / x)` as `x * (exp(S/x) - exp(-S/x)) / (exp(S/x) + exp(-S/x))`. Both exponentials overflow to `inf` when `|S / x| > ~88`, so the ratio becomes `inf / inf = NaN` and the whole attention row is poisoned.

This is reachable for Gemma-2 style models that set `attn_logit_softcapping = 50`: a pre-softcap score above 4400 overflows. These models have very large attention logits, which is why they use softcapping. Verified on a GTX 1650 Ti with the real helper:

```text
input  : [1.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 3000.0, 5000.0, 10000.0, -1.0, -10000.0, 4400.0]
before : [0.9999, 48.2, 50.0, 50.0, NaN, NaN, -0.9999, NaN, inf]
after  : [0.9999, 48.2, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, -0.9999, -50.0, 50.0]
```

The fix computes the same value as `1 - 2 / (exp(2 * S / x) + 1)`, which saturates cleanly at `+/-1` for either sign. The helper is shared by the unified, DiffKV, and INT4 attention kernels.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k softcap_does_not_overflow_on_large_scores
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k "50.0 and not fp8 and not q_dtype1"
```

## Test Result

- New test fails on main without the fix: `NaN` for the large scores.
- With the fix: the new test passes.
- 336 softcap tests pass. The `fp8` cases fail only on SM75, where Triton reports `fp8e4nv` is unsupported.
